key_highlights: RBA issues blunt warning ahead of next rate decision; IMF urges spending cuts as another hike looms (#25, #75)
ASX ends volatile week with modest gains as oil prices and bond yields ease; big four banks advance (#34, #52)
Recession odds for 2027 rise amid petrol price shock, Middle East oil shock, and soaring state interest costs (#32, #39, #68, #73)
Iron ore prices under pressure; Japan diverts Australian LNG to East Coast starved of supply (#35, #36)
Fed raises rates for first time in three years on diesel/gas surge, pressuring global risk assets (#64)
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, boosting tech/infrastructure sentiment (#78)
WA gold sector active: Forrestania prefeasibility studies and Aurum Côte d'Ivoire high-grade discovery (#22, #31)
Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman at 96, marking generational shift in global investing (#4)
Qantas ground staff strike looms over Joyce-era bargaining; Coles keeps milk prices elevated (#47, #50)
Housing affordability at record lows; tenants see some relief but structural pressure persists (#40, #67)

sectors.trend: Iron ore prices under sustained pressure ('roaches seethe'); LNG pricing distorted by Japan diverting Australian gas. Gold sector active with Forrestania and Aurum discoveries. Coal policy uncertainty under Albo government.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from soft iron ore. Woodside (WDS.AX) and Santos (STO.AX) benefit from LNG scarcity premium. Gold miners (NVL.AX, GRY.AX) supported by safe-haven flows. Coal exposure (BLL.AX, WDS.AX coal segment) faces policy risk.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advance on easing yields and oil prices. RBA warning and IMF spending-cut pressure signal tighter monetary path. State governments face soaring interest costs, pressuring sovereign credit.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from wider NIMs if RBA hikes. Bendigo Bank (BGB.AX) faces structural headwinds from Adelaide-based job cuts. Superannuation reform debate (#2) could reshape fund flows.

sectors.trend: Middle East oil shock and Fed rate hike on diesel/gas surge create volatile energy backdrop. Petrol price shock hits consumer sentiment. Victoria retreats from renewable transmission, favouring fossil fuel continuity.
sectors.implications: SAP.AX, WDS.AX, STO.AX see near-term support from oil/LNG prices. Renewable names (LVR.AX, GPP.AX) face policy headwind from Victoria's transmission retreat. Petrol shock pressures transport and consumer discretionary.

sectors.trend: Global biotech mixed: Cellectis exits CAR-T programs, Vaxcyte nears pivotal trial. No major ASX-listed healthcare catalysts today.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. ASX-listed biotech (e.g., ACH.AX, NHC.AX) track global sentiment. No direct ASX impact from US biotech headlines.

sectors.trend: Coles maintains elevated milk prices despite axing farmer support. Petrol shock and housing unaffordability squeeze household budgets. Qantas strike threat disrupts travel.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WSG.AX face margin pressure from input costs. QAN.AX exposed to strike risk. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) relatively resilient but margin compression likely.

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn Queensland datacentre deal signals major capex cycle. AI adoption debate continues. ASX small-caps (Latrobe, CurveBeam, Arrow, Sultan) show relative strength.
sectors.implications: Datacentre/infrastructure names (SGH.AX, VMC.AX) benefit from AI capex. Small-cap momentum in tech/energy exploration supports speculative flows.

sectors.trend: Housing at 'absurdly unaffordable' levels; tenants see marginal relief. Rising interest costs pressure state and corporate borrowing. No major ASX REIT catalysts.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face higher financing costs. Residential property (MRG.AX, LVH.AX) constrained by affordability ceiling.

key_themes: Monetary tightening cycle: RBA warning + IMF pressure + Fed hike = higher-for-longer rates
Commodity volatility: iron ore weakness vs LNG scarcity premium vs Middle East oil shock
Fiscal stress: state interest costs soaring, IMF urging federal spending cuts
Energy transition friction: Victoria retreats from renewables, coal policy uncertainty
AI infrastructure supercycle: $31bn Anthropic deal signals sustained capex
Consumer squeeze: petrol shock, housing unaffordability, Coles pricing
Global risk-off: Buffett succession, recession odds rising, China re-rating
Labour disputes: Qantas strike, Bendigo cuts, working holiday visa limits

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds, reduce leverage, favour rate-sensitive banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX) with strong NIMs
Maintain defensive allocation (CSL.AX, WES.AX, WOW.AX), reduce cyclical exposure, hold 15-20% cash

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / petrol price spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge fuel exposure, favour energy producers (SAP.AX, WDS.AX), avoid transport/consumer discretionary
Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weightings; rotate into gold (NVL.AX) and LNG (WDS.AX, STO.AX)
Avoid QAN.AX ahead of strike; monitor airline sector contagion
Underweight residential REITs; favour industrial/office REITs with contracted tenancies
Monitor state bond spreads; favour federal infrastructure beneficiaries

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners on safe-haven and inflation-hedge flows
opportunities.rationale: Recession odds rising, Middle East oil shock, and Fed hike support gold; Forrestania and Aurum discoveries add sector catalysts

opportunities.recommendation: Add LNG-exposed energy names on supply scarcity premium
opportunities.rationale: Japan diverting Australian gas creates pricing power; Middle East oil shock supports broader energy complex

opportunities.recommendation: Position in AI infrastructure / datacentre beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: $31bn Anthropic Queensland deal signals multi-year capex cycle; ASX small-cap tech showing relative strength

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight big four banks on rate hike cycle
opportunities.rationale: RBA warning and IMF pressure signal further hikes; banks advance on easing yields; NIM expansion likely

defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore under pressure; coal policy risk under Albo government; China demand uncertainty
Petrol shock, housing unaffordability, and Qantas strike threaten household spending and airline operations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Increase cash / short-duration bond allocation to 15-20%
defensive_moves.rationale: Recession odds rising, RBA hike imminent, volatile week signals elevated uncertainty

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight residential REITs and property developers
defensive_moves.rationale: Housing at 'absurdly unaffordable' levels; rising interest costs pressure valuations and demand

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and range-bound. RBA rate decision and IMF pressure create headwinds, but bank strength and energy pricing provide partial support. Petrol shock and Middle East oil risk could trigger sharp intraday moves. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a tight range with elevated VIX. Small-cap momentum (Latrobe, CurveBeam) may fade.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Rising 2027 recession odds, structural housing unaffordability, and fiscal stress cap upside. However, AI infrastructure capex (Anthropic deal), gold strength, and LNG pricing provide sector-specific opportunities. A soft-landing scenario requires RBA to pause after one more hike and oil prices to stabilise. Base case: ^AXJO consolidates 8,200-8,800 with sector rotation into defensives.
